authors: Smith, W. L. and Wilkinson, W. E.
title: On Branching Processes in Random Environments
annotation: Shows that a Galton-Watson process in an i.i.d. random environment dies out with probability one exactly when the expected log of the mean offspring number is not positive.

authors: Athreya, K. B. and Karlin, S.
title: On Branching Processes with Random Environments: I: Extinction Probabilities
annotation: Extends the extinction criterion for branching processes to stationary ergodic environments, where the sign of the typical log growth decides extinction.

title: A Formula Connecting Sample and Moment Stability of Linear Stochastic Systems
annotation: Relates the growth rates of the moments of a linear stochastic system to its almost-sure Lyapunov exponent through the convex moment Lyapunov function.

title: On the Convergence of Ordinary Integrals to Stochastic Integrals
annotation: Shows that ordinary differential equations driven by smooth approximations of Brownian motion converge to the Stratonovich stochastic differential equation.

title: Threshold Dynamics for Compartmental Epidemic Models in Periodic Environments
venue: Journal of Dynamics and Differential Equations 20, 699-717
annotation: Defines the basic reproduction number for compartmental epidemic models with periodic coefficients and proves that it is the invasion threshold.

authors: Gray, A. and Greenhalgh, D. and Hu, L. and Mao, X. and Pan, J.
title: A Stochastic Differential Equation SIS Epidemic Model
annotation: Perturbs the transmission rate of the SIS model by white noise and shows that the almost-sure extinction threshold falls below the deterministic reproduction number.

authors: Gray, A. and Greenhalgh, D. and Mao, X. and Pan, J.
title: The SIS epidemic model with Markovian switching
venue: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications 394, 496-516
annotation: Switches the rates of the SIS model by a finite Markov chain and shows that almost-sure extinction or persistence is decided by the stationary average of the per-capita growth rate, not by the reproduction number of the mean system.

authors: Hernandez-Suarez, C. and Rabinovich, J. and Hernandez, K.
title: The long-run distribution of births across environments under environmental stochasticity and its use in the calculation of unconditional life-history parameters
annotation: Computes life-history parameters averaged over a Markovian environment, including a reproduction parameter that governs growth of the expected population.

title: On the basic reproduction number in a random environment
annotation: Defines a reproduction number for populations in a Markovian random environment whose position relative to one decides growth or decay of typical populations, and contrasts it with a parameter for the expected population.

authors: Benaïm, M. and Le Borgne, S. and Malrieu, F. and Zitt, P.-A.
title: On the stability of planar randomly switched systems
annotation: Shows that random switching between two stable planar linear systems can produce an unstable system, depending on the switching rate.

authors: Li, D. and Liu, S. and Cui, J.
title: Threshold dynamics and ergodicity of an SIRS epidemic model with Markovian switching
annotation: Gives the extinction and persistence threshold of an SIRS model whose rates switch with a Markov chain, as a stationary average over regimes.

title: Large population asymptotics for a multitype stochastic SIS epidemic model in randomly switching environment
annotation: Studies a multitype stochastic SIS epidemic in a switching environment and shows that the sign of the top Lyapunov exponent of the linearized switched system governs the time to extinction.

title: Asymptotic expansion of the invariant measure for Markov-modulated ODEs at high frequency
annotation: Expands the invariant measure of ordinary differential equations modulated by a fast Markov chain in powers of the switching time, with a first-order formula for the top Lyapunov exponent of switched linear systems.

authors: Monmarché, P. and Schreiber, S. J. and Strickler, É.
title: Impacts of Tempo and Mode of Environmental Fluctuations on Population Growth: Slow- and Fast-Limit Approximations of Lyapunov Exponents for Periodic and Random Environments
annotation: Gives first-order slow- and fast-switching approximations of the Lyapunov exponent of structured populations switched periodically or by a Markov chain, the closest prior work to the almost-sure formula here.
